title: Climate Change and the Cost of Food

paragraphs.en: Extreme weather, from floods to droughts, is becoming more frequent, and farmers are feeling the consequences in their fields and their finances.
paragraphs.zh: 从洪水到干旱，极端天气正变得更加频繁，农民们正在田间和财务上感受到由此带来的后果。

paragraphs.en: When harvests fail, the price of staples such as wheat and rice climbs. Poor households, which spend a large share of their income on food, are hit hardest.
paragraphs.zh: 当收成失败时，小麦和大米等主食的价格就会攀升。那些将收入的大部分用于食品的贫困家庭受到的影响最为严重。

paragraphs.en: Climate models predict that heatwaves and irregular rainfall will reduce yields in many regions by mid-century, even as the global population continues to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 气候模型预测，到本世纪中叶，热浪和不规律的降雨将降低许多地区的产量，即便全球人口仍在持续增长。

paragraphs.en: Some countries are responding by breeding crops that tolerate heat and drought. Others are investing in irrigation and better storage to reduce losses after harvest.
paragraphs.zh: 一些国家正在通过培育耐热耐旱的作物来应对。另一些国家则在投资灌溉和更好的储存设施，以减少收获后的损失。

paragraphs.en: Adaptation alone will not be enough. Scientists insist that cutting greenhouse-gas emissions remains essential to prevent the worst outcomes for global food security.
paragraphs.zh: 仅靠适应是不够的。科学家们坚持认为，削减温室气体排放对于防止全球粮食安全出现最坏结果仍然至关重要。

paragraphs.en: The challenge is one of fairness as well as science. Those who contributed least to climate change are often those who will suffer most from its effects on agriculture.
paragraphs.zh: 这一挑战既关乎科学，也关乎公平。对气候变化贡献最少的国家，往往是在其对农业的影响中受害最深的。
